observation.visible_scene: A wide shot of a calm, rippled body of water bordered by a steep, densely forested rock cliff. A low band of white mist/fog hovers just above the waterline at the base of the cliff. In the foreground a log boom (a raft of long floating logs) runs diagonally across the lower half of the frame. Several small birds (light/white and dark) are perched on the logs, and a small yellow-green object (buoy/marker) sits on the boom near the middle. The view appears to be taken from a moving platform (boat).
visible_changes: Over the excerpt the entire foreground arrangement (log boom, perched birds, yellow marker) and the mist band drift steadily toward the left edge of the frame, while the cliff/trees also shift slightly left, indicating a continuous camera translation/pan rather than the logs themselves moving across the water.
The diagonal angle of the log boom flattens a little (becomes more horizontal) as the viewpoint changes, consistent with parallax from camera motion.
The perched birds remain on the logs throughout, with only minor posture/position adjustments relative to the logs; they do not fly off or arrive.
The mist layer subtly thickens/thins and shifts shape near the cliff base, and the water surface shows continuous small ripples.
No new objects enter and none leave except by drifting out of the left frame edge.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the camera platform (boat) started or stops moving outside this segment is unknown.
The cause of the mist and the origin/destination of the log boom are not shown.
Whether the birds arrived or departed the boom is outside the clip.
uncertain_details: Exact bird species and the identity of the yellow-green object on the logs are not determinable.
The relative contribution of camera pan vs. boat translation, and any independent drift of the mist vs. apparent motion from camera movement, cannot be fully separated.
The yellow marker's slight apparent shift may be camera parallax rather than its own motion.
